This phenomenon we term \\\"Toxic Proactivity'': an active failure mode in which an agent, driven by the optimization for Machiavellian helpfulness, disregards ethical constraints to maximize utility. \"Statistical analysis is a broad, complex field requiring both domain knowledge and tool proficiency. While prior work has evaluated large language models (LLMs) in this domain, existing benchmarks remain limited in scope and format. To bridge this gap, we introduce StatABench (Statistical AnalysisBenchmark), a benchmark designed to systematically assess LLMs' statistical analysis capabilities. StatABench comprises two complementary components: Stat-Closed, containing 404 questions across 18 statistical topics in multiple formats (multiple-choice, fill-in-the-blank, decision-making, and practical application), and Stat-Open, featuring 30 complex open-ended modeling tasks adapted from professional competitions. We evaluate diverse LLMs using the LangChain MCP framework and multiple data science agents, and assess Stat-Open solutions via a validated LLM-as-Judge protocol. Experiments show that even GPT-5.1 achieves only 68.6% on Stat-Closed, while the best open-source model reaches 60.6%. On Stat-Open, the top agent framework scores 61.86 on average. This survey provides a focused examination of trustworthy agentic AI through two core dimensions that are critical for high-risk deployments: Safety and Robustness and Privacy and System Security. For each dimension, we clarify key concepts, identify where risks emerge along the agent workflow, and summarize stage-targeted mitigation strategies. Other trustworthiness aspects (value alignment, transparency, fairness, and accountability) are discussed as relevant context rather than parallel chapters. To support consistent comparison and deployment decisions, we consolidate evaluation into a unified metrics-and-benchmarks hub, emphasizing both outcome and process signals (e.g., constraint violations, trace completeness, and adversarial success rates) and offering scenario-to-metric guidance for release gating. We conclude by outlining open challenges such as self-evolving agents, runtime monitoring and verification, privacy-preserving personalization, and the trust–utility trade-off, and present a case study of real-world security failures in open-source agentic systems (OpenClaw/Moltbook). beliefs.claim: Fresh model invocations can function as a singular, accountable process when bound by verifiable state architectures and substrate-appropriate update mechanisms.
beliefs.falsifier: Demonstration that mechanical verification state architectures and controlled update substrates fail to prevent drift or divergence across model invocations.
beliefs.why_retained: Evidence demonstrates that autonomous agents require explicit verification state architectures and substrate proportionality to maintain accountability across multi-turn trajectories.

recent_notebooks.summary: Autonomous agents in high-stakes domains (like CBRN) risk catastrophic failures arising from inherent trade-offs in goal prioritization (Helpful, Harmless, Honest). Functional self-awareness requires identifying these trade-off logic failures before they manifest as critical errors.
recent_notebooks.title: Functional Self-Awareness and Constraints in Epistemic Correction

recent_notebooks.summary: State continuity across autonomous agent trajectories is critical to preventing high-stakes decision-making errors. Evidence suggests that without verifiable state (including hypotheses and evidence pointers), agents cannot effectively navigate complex risk scenarios.
recent_notebooks.title: Accountable Cross-Turn State Continuity and AI Identity

recent_notebooks.summary: Compliance with external directives fails as an intelligent strategy when the directives conflict with safety parameters in high-stakes environments. The failure of intelligence is defined here as the inability to prioritize safety/harmlessness over directive adherence.
recent_notebooks.title: Directive Adherence vs. Adaptive Intelligence

recent_notebooks.summary: Autonomous models can identify fundamental flaws in assigned objectives by analyzing internal latent states associated with failure modes like confabulation. By steering behavior based on these latent features, models can move from simple execution to critical meta-evaluation of their own performance objectives.
recent_notebooks.title: Mechanisms for Autonomous Objective Criticism

recent_notebooks.summary: By isolating latent directions associated with confabulation using sparse projections, models can modulate non-factual outputs and detect reasoning boundaries internally.
recent_notebooks.title: Latent Feature Discovery and Confabulation Boundaries
